source.title: Poly-time universality and limitations of deep learning

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses prior work on generalization and reports an experiment on structured parity labels, but does not test random-label fitting or another listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a parity-image experiment: SGD fits the training set but does not generalize better than chance. This is not random labeling. Its theoretical discussion of learning random functions and its citations to prior results are not empirical results about fitting random labels.
record.test_reason: The experiment measures fitting and generalization on deterministic parity labels, not completely random labels. The theoretical results concern prediction on fresh samples, with specialized initializations or noise and memory constraints; they do not establish or refute any listed version about training-set memorization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the parity experiment, but not the paper's main conclusion. The authors prove that suitably constructed and initialized networks trained with SGD can emulate efficient learning algorithms, while noisy full or sufficiently large-batch GD has generalization limitations on low-cross-predictability function distributions. The parity experiment illustrates fitting without generalization under random initialization.
record.recipe_differences: The experiment uses parity labels on generated images, not random labels on a training set; it reports no label-randomization intervention.

fits_no_version.finding: A randomly initialized three-hidden-layer ReLU perceptron trained with SGD fits a finite parity-image training set while test accuracy remains at chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-set fitting can coexist with chance generalization on a deterministic parity-image task.

record.problems: The experiment reports no numerical training or test errors, uncertainty estimates, or comparison condition. It uses a single generated parity task and does not test random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results omitted. Theoretical statements about arbitrary efficiently learnable function distributions and cited prior results do not report outcomes for random-label fitting.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random training labels to near-zero error with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, with test performance at chance.
Training-time comparison between true and random labels, and convergence as label corruption increases.
Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs using the same networks.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across random-label corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and of their removal on true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: Random parity functions retain deterministic structure and are not independent random label assignments. Random labels used in the theoretical null model define a comparison process; no training-set fitting result is reported for that process. Neither those arguments nor the parity experiment yields a verdict on V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random training labels; chance test error under those labels; unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across fractions of randomly corrupted labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, or augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real-data patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: 3 hidden linear layer perceptron with 128 units and ReLU non linearities
rows.operation_detail: Trained with binary cross entropy using PyTorch SGD on parity-labeled images.
rows.measure: Training-set fit and test generalization on images labeled by parity of black dots.
rows.value: The net can learn the training set but does not generalize better than random guessing.
rows.note: Parity labels are structured, not random labels. The text does not give numerical training or test error values.
rows.check: The reported parity-task result is accurate but cannot determine any claim version. Labels follow the parity of the image's black squares. The setup uses 1,000 training images and 1,000 testing images; the baseline for test performance is 50% accuracy. The supplied figure text does not permit precise numerical endpoint extraction.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
